identity.real_world_identity_notes: The exact RaceRoom content is the Renault Laguna Super Touring listed for 1998. It belongs to the Williams Renault BTCC / Super Touring Laguna family: contemporary and period-specific material identifies a front-wheel-drive 2.0-litre touring car using a six-speed sequential Hewland gearbox operated by a tall sequential stick. A period driver account says the running upchanges needed no clutch but did require a throttle lift; it does not establish the downshift, standing-start clutch, gearbox construction, or exact steering-rim topology for the 1998 simulator identity.

RaceRoom's official catalogue names the exact content Renault Laguna Super Touring and lists 1998, Super Touring, 2.0L four-cylinder, and front-wheel drive. RM Sotheby's identifies a Williams-prepared Renault Laguna Super Touring that competed in the 1998 BTCC and used a six-speed sequential transmission. A contemporary-driver account identifies the Laguna's six-speed Hewland sequential stick and directly describes clutchless upchanges with a required throttle lift. The checked-out repository has no existing record for this exact identity, so the proposal creates a new record.

claims.basis: RaceRoom's official catalogue names the exact content Renault Laguna Super Touring and lists 1998, Super Touring, 2.0L four-cylinder, and front-wheel drive. RM Sotheby's identifies a Williams-prepared Renault Laguna Super Touring that competed in the 1998 BTCC and used a six-speed sequential transmission. A contemporary-driver account identifies the Laguna's six-speed Hewland sequential stick and directly describes clutchless upchanges with a required throttle lift. The checked-out repository has no existing record for this exact identity, so the proposal creates a new record.

The period competition record and the driver account both describe a six-speed Laguna sequential gearbox; a later Williams Laguna listing independently specifies a six-speed Hewland sequential gearbox. Coulthard describes a tall gear lever with direct push/pull sequential action, and the period car listing corroborates the six-speed sequential transmission. Both sources describe the six forward ratios as a sequential gearbox; Coulthard also records the push-forward/pull-back sequential pattern. Direct driver testimony about the Williams Renault Laguna states that running upchanges needed no clutch. The source is an earlier Laguna test rather than a chassis-numbered 1998 car, so confidence is medium rather than high. The same driver testimony explicitly says the driver had to lift off during the upchange and could not power-shift the Laguna. The source is an earlier Laguna test rather than a chassis-numbered 1998 car, so confidence is medium. The sourced running-upshift procedure is a lift-and-shift action; it does not call for a driver rev-match blip on an upshift. The sourced running-upshift procedure contains no automatic throttle-blip action; blipping is a downshift technique, not an upshift requirement. The source's explicit throttle-lift instruction applies to the running upshift; it does not prescribe a distinct throttle-lift technique for downshift. The available source discusses the upshift lift requirement and provides no downshift torque-cut procedure; this field is not established as a downshift action.
